title: Greedy Best-First in Alfama: Chase the Shortest!
description: Watch Greedy Best-First race across Lisbon’s Alfama streets using a heuristic to aggressively pick the next best-looking node. The visualization shows how local “promising” choices can find fast paths—and sometimes miss the truly optimal route.
ig_caption:
🚶‍♂️✨ **Greedy Best-First** powering a street-map path in **Alfama, Lisbon**!

In this visualization, each intersection is a **node** and each road segment is an **edge**, forming a real-world **graph**. Greedy Best-First expands the next node using only the **heuristic** (here, distance-to-go from the current node to the goal), choosing the lowest estimated cost first—so it *feels* like it’s “chasing” the destination. 🧠📍

⚙️ **Key idea (graph theory):** we maintain a priority queue ordered by **h(n)**, not by the full path cost. That means it’s **informed search**, but typically **not guaranteed optimal** because it ignores the accumulated travel cost g(n).
